title: Frontend: List Sorter
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind List Sorter. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Parse comma-separated finite numbers from Numbers, trim each, and return an ascending sorted copy, retaining duplicates. Blank means empty array. Invalid entries show Invalid numbers. Render controlled labelled inputs with these exact names: Numbers. A Calculate submit button computes the result. Render JSON.stringify(result) in [data-testid="result"]. Validation failure clears result and shows the documented message in [data-testid="error"].
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Store only sort configuration and derive a copied sorted array.
alternativeApproaches: Move sorting to a paginated server and keep its ordering and tie-breakers consistent with cursor pagination.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Equal keys; numeric-looking strings; null values.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
